text:
I booked via there Facebook page from New Zealand to have 7 white crowns crowns,(2 x bridges). Everything from start to finish was excellent, from the professional receptionists and the attentive dentist. Very friendly too.
I felt no pain during or post. The cost for all the work including the temporary teeth were around $3500 NZ,  the price was competitive compared to the fancy looking frontage dentists you will see in Koh Samui.
Thank you to the team not only did you do a great job you have given me confidence not having to wear a denture anymore.

text: Excellent - Teeth whitening. Could not be more happy. They squeezed me in a short notice last minute appointment. Receptionists, dentist and all staff were very professional. Would recommend.

I had a similarly bad experience here. I called on Thursday with a severe toothache, of course I didn't get an appointment straight away and was put off until Sunday. On Saturday I got a call asking me to come on Sunday. There was another call on Sunday two hours before the appointment. The doctor supposedly had an accident with his car and didn't have time today. Of course it was a wonderful day, so I can imagine that you'd rather go to the beach with your family than treat a patient with a toothache. Of course I didn't make another appointment. That's just not how you treat patients

No integrity whatsoever. After agreeing to a set price and speaking directly to the dentist I was advised that my general clean and polish that I have annually back home suddenly went up 400 baht upon arriving on time whilst sitting in the dentists chair. Very poor and misleading particularly when I asked to speak to  the dentist directly prior to arriving. I will not recommend friends who will be arriving on the island who need considerable amount of work. This is the first time I have had to walk out from a business based on principles and thought I would share my experience.

Very professional, I've been there twice already.

The staff is very friendly. …

Terrible clinic. They say they're open, but in reality, there's just one bored receptionist who can't really explain anything. I understand there are no doctors on site. I was constantly calling someone.
My problem was that a veneer on my front tooth fell off. I wanted to replace it. Eventually, the receptionist showed me the price list and, for some reason, started referring me to Bangkok Samui Hospital. Basically, it's some kind of underground lab! I don't recommend visiting.

Oh... it must be the peculiarities of island life. It's some kind of complicated clinic... they always open when needed, so they're not open. Well, actually, they are open—the secretary is there... but when something is especially urgent, they always have an appointment scheduled for "Thursday," when it could be Friday or Sunday.

Even when you have a scheduled appointment, they always call and try to screw things up and reschedule your "convenient time" for "their convenient time."

We had a great experience visiting them.

My wife got braces there. The next day after they were installed, the braces fell off one of her teeth.
It was Friday, midday, business hours.
We called the clinic, and it was impossible to explain anything in English, but it was clear they were still open and we could come by (they wouldn't have a doctor until Thursday). We finally arrived. The secretary looked at her, and her face showed "aaah, so that's what it is." She said, "I'll make an appointment for Thursday, the doctor's gone to Surat." 🤦🏼
So my wife spent a week with broken braces because the doctor was in Surat until Thursday.

The jokes about calling and rescheduling appointments also apply to braces. They need to be adjusted every month. So, in a year and a half, it hasn't happened even once (!) When they didn't call the day before to reschedule, it eventually became annoying and they simply stopped answering the phone. So, during the visit, the secretary asks, "Is this your number? I called and couldn't get through." (Is this even normal?! - Maybe only in the countryside.)

I had a similar story myself. I chipped a tooth at dinner on Saturday. 8 PM - nothing's open, of course.
I went to the clinic on Sunday. It's supposedly business hours. I thought they'd fix the situation, but it's the same story at the clinic. I described the problem, and they said, "Well, let me make an appointment for Thursday." Of course, I'm not in a rush. "Can you tell me, please, what about a Thursday in February or March?" 🤦🏼
Meanwhile, there's no line in the clinic; all the offices are empty. The appointment book only has 1-2 appointments a day.

The doctor himself (a man) seems okay, at least by the standards of this village. But the way they work is terrible and atrocious.
